title: Pair-extraction machine
statement: For each pair of Boolean parameters $(f,s)$, there is a deterministic Boolean Turing machine with one work tape and state set $\mathrm{Option}(\mathrm{Option}(\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\})\oplus\mathrm{Fin}(3))$, initially in the state representing no stored Boolean. Its transition function is the following: in the initial state it moves right through the input, storing the first symbol in its state, and halts if it encounters blank. With a stored Boolean $b$, it moves right on the next input symbol $c$: if $b=c$, it writes $b$ on the work tape and enters the initial state; if $b\ne c$ and $b$ is true, it halts; if $b\ne c$ and $b$ is false, it moves the work-tape head left and enters phase $0$. In phase $0$, it moves the work-tape head left over occupied cells, then right into phase $1$ at a blank cell. In phase $1$, it moves the work-tape head right over occupied cells, writing the scanned symbol to the output exactly when $f$ is true; at a blank cell it enters phase $2$. In phase $2$, if $s$ is true, it moves right along the input, emitting each scanned symbol, and halts on blank; if $s$ is false, it halts immediately. All transitions not specified as emitting a symbol emit nothing, and omitted successor states halt.
